claim: The chapter's Speaking Practice NOTES rule (a noun made the topic takes は in place of を or が, and moves to the head of the sentence) appears in two cards but is explained on none.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE NOTES: "When the word that is the topic has the particles が or を, they change to は. When the particle is other than が or を, は is added." and "ばんごはん has been made the topic, so the particle を has changed to は, and ばんごはん comes at the head of the sentence." Cards chan-likes-steak-topic (エマさん、ステーキはすきですか) and supper-before-or-after-meeting (ばんごはんはかいぎのまえにたべますか。あとでたべますか) both ship with no note. No earlier card in the ledger explains を becoming は.
fix: Add a note to supper-before-or-after-meeting (and a short one to chan-likes-steak-topic) saying ばんごはんを becomes ばんごはんは when it is the topic, and the topic moves to the front.

claim: GRAMMAR 2's rule that after a verb of movement the second action happens at the place you went is shown on a card with the book's own example, but no back explains it.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "when the first clause uses a verb of movement such as いきます, きます, or かえります, the location of the action of the second clause is assumed to be the same, even if not stated explicitly ... きのう ぎんざに いって、ひるごはんを たべました ... The place where I ate lunch was Ginza." Card went-ginza-ate-lunch: きのうぎんざにいって、ひるごはんをたべました / 'Yesterday I went to Ginza and ate lunch there.' with no note.
fix: Add a note to went-ginza-ate-lunch: after いって (or きて, かえって) the next action is understood to happen at that place, so no で phrase is needed.

claim: GRAMMAR 2's restriction that clauses differing in mood or tense cannot be joined with the て-form is not on any card.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "if the moods and tenses of the clauses are not the same, they cannot be linked using the て-form", with the example of a statement (チケットが ２まい あります) and a suggestion (あした いっしょに えいがを みませんか) that cannot be joined. No card in chapter-18 or chapter-18-extras mentions it; the nearest is answer-osaka-branch-presentation's note "The tense is set only by the last verb".
fix: Extend the note on answer-osaka-branch-presentation (or ginza-then-meet-friend) by one sentence: two clauses of different kinds, such as a statement and an invitation, are not joined with て.

claim: The card renders Exercise VI item 2 in the non-past, but the item follows the book's past-tense example and calls for the past.
evidence: Book, Exercise VI: "e.g. 2. きのう パーティーが ありました。パーティーの あと、タクシーで うちに かえりました。 2. (バーに いって、ウイスキーを のみます)", with the instruction to use "the appropriate forms". Card: パーティーのあと、バーにいって、ウイスキーをのみます / 'After the party, I will go to a bar and drink whiskey.'
fix: Change the target to パーティーのあと、バーにいって、ウイスキーをのみました and the English to 'After the party, I went to a bar and drank whiskey.'

claim: The note calls Lesson 16's ちょっと 'casual', which the book does not say; the book presents it as a polite, indirect refusal.
evidence: Card note: "It is more formal than the casual ちょっと (chotto) \"Well, it's a bit...\" from Lesson 16". Book, Lesson 16 GRAMMAR: "は ちょっと … is added when responding to an inconvenient date ... or to invitations you are reluctant to accept ... because of the Japanese tendency to avoid a clear refusal." The deck's own Lesson 16 card reads 'Well, it's a bit... (used to decline politely)'.
fix: Drop the word 'casual' and the formality comparison; say instead that here ちょっと means 'a moment', not the polite refusal from Lesson 16.

claim: The note names a contrast-pair card that does not ship: both 'listen' halves of the pair were excluded at gate 2.
evidence: Card kiku-ask note: "Contrast pair with おんがくをきいてください (ongaku o kiite kudasai)." Card kiku-ongaku (おんがくをきいてください) and kiku-listen-pair (ラジオでニュースをきいてください) are both excluded with excludedBy gate2-frame-trim.
fix: Reword the note to contrast with a shipping card, for example link-kiite-tegami (おんがくをきいて、てがみをかきます), or drop the pair reference.
